metadata.prompt:
Cinematic movie poster for a 30-second gangster thriller short. 16:9 anamorphic frame, 2048x1152. Vast abandoned concrete warehouse at night, exposed ductwork in shadows. Single bare tungsten bulb hanging from ceiling on frayed wire, casting harsh amber pool of light over a scarred metal table, everything beyond lost in deep teal-black shadow. Foreground left: back of a man in black zip jacket, short dark hair, standing still, facing the table. Behind table sits older silver-haired man in dark charcoal suit, leaned back in wooden chair, half face in deep shadow, only eyes catching light, silver signet ring glinting on right hand. On table: open brushed-aluminum briefcase, black-and-white photographs fanned out, crystal ashtray with lit cigarette sending up thin smoke, two lowball glasses of amber liquor. Thick smoke drifts through amber light beam. Large shaved-head bodyguard in dark coat stands silhouette behind the older man's right shoulder. Teal-and-orange grade: crushed teal shadows, warm tungsten amber highlights. 35mm anamorphic lens: oval bokeh, horizontal lens flare, edge softness, heavy film grain, halation. Neo-noir, low-key lighting.

Large bold condensed sans-serif Chinese title "正午" centered lower third, white with subtle amber glow and grain. Above title smaller clean Chinese sans-serif: "Seedance 2.5 测试短片". Below title small spaced Chinese: "30秒连续正反打 · 真人级微表情 · 35mm变形宽银幕".

metadata.prompt:
30-second photorealistic crime thriller. Continuity editing: three shots connected by motivated hard cuts. Same abandoned concrete warehouse throughout. Same single bare hanging tungsten bulb as the only key light. Continuous ambient sound bed across all cuts. Eyeline matches between characters. 35mm anamorphic 2.39:1, shallow depth of field, heavy film grain, 24fps, teal-and-amber grade with crushed blacks. Natural, imperfect, lived-in human beings. No plastic skin. No glowing eyes. No sci-fi elements.

[Reference image 1: JAX and four men standing, facing camera]
[Reference image 2: VOR seated behind metal table, bodyguard behind him]

CHARACTERS — photorealistic skin with visible pores, subsurface scattering, five-o'clock shadow, slight asymmetry, natural imperfections, capillaries, slight oil on forehead, lips slightly dry:
JAX: 32, white male, short dark brown hair, square jaw, light stubble, pale blue eyes, black zip jacket over dark gray tee. Poised coiled stillness. Natural blink rate every 3-5 seconds. Eyes do not glow or change color.
FOUR MEN behind JAX in loose wedge: short dark hair in black hoodie; wavy brown hair in olive shirt; short dark hair in dark pullover; shaved-head bearded in dark jacket. Half in shadow, minimal natural movement.
VOR: 60s, white male, silver combed-back hair, deep facial lines, hooded heavy-lidded eyes, dark charcoal suit over black shirt no tie, silver signet ring on his right ring finger. Leaned back in old wooden chair behind table. Posture of a man who has sat in this chair a thousand times.
BODYGUARD: large shaved-head man in dark wool coat behind VOR's right shoulder, hands clasped in front of him, face in near silhouette.

PROPS on heavy scarred metal table: open brushed-aluminum briefcase with a blank, unengraved machined aluminum nameplate inside the lid; several black-and-white photographs fanned out; heavy crystal ashtray with one lit cigarette sending up a thin curl of smoke; two lowball glasses of amber liquor, untouched; a Zippo lighter sitting closed beside the ashtray. That is all. No phones. No radios. No screens. No timers. No digital readouts. No blinking lights. No wires. No electronic devices of any kind.

CAMERA LANGUAGE: Locked-off tripods with almost imperceptibly slow push-ins. No zooms. No whip pans. No rack-focus-through-bodies. Hard cuts are standard shot/reverse-shot coverage — the grammar of Heat and The Godfather. The camera is patient. Stillness is tension. Less is more.

[0:00-0:10] SHOT 1 — MEDIUM SHOT, eye level, JAX and four men. Based on reference image 1.
Locked camera, very slow push-in barely visible. JAX stands center frame facing camera, feet shoulder-width, hands loosely at sides. The four men form a loose wedge behind him, faces half in shadow. In the deep background VOR is an out-of-focus silhouette behind the table; a tiny orange cigarette ember glows there in the dark.
Only natural movement: dust motes drifting in the amber light shaft, the lit cigarette smoke rising from the ashtray on the table behind, the men breathing with visible breath in cold air, the bulb swaying millimeters shifting shadows. JAX blinks naturally. His gaze is steady on the lens.
At 0:03 JAX speaks, lips parting just enough, voice low and controlled: "You said noon." A beat. Jaw shifts slightly. "It's twelve." He does not raise his voice. Behind him the wavy-haired man's gaze drops then rises. The shaved-head man's index finger twitches once at his side.
JAX finishes. Lips close. Tongue presses inside his cheek half a second then releases.
SOUND: Deep sub-bass drone felt more than heard. Distant water drip every 4 seconds. Bulb filament hum. Nasal breathing of the men. Close-mic'd dialogue with natural concrete reverb RT60 about 1.2 seconds. No music.

[0:10] HARD CUT TO:

[0:10-0:20] SHOT 2 — MEDIUM SHOT, slightly low angle, VOR at table. Based on reference image 2.
Sound bridge: ambient room tone and JAX's last word carry across the cut without a break — same space, same air.
Locked camera, slow push-in. VOR sits leaned back in the wooden chair, right ankle resting on his left knee under the table, hands interlaced over his stomach. Top light carves deep nasolabial shadows and leaves his eye sockets dark. Bodyguard stands statue-still behind his right shoulder, hands clasped. On the table the open briefcase shows the blank nameplate catching amber light — held in view for two seconds as the camera pushes. Cigarette smoke from the ashtray curls up between VOR and lens. The Zippo sits closed and untouched on the table.
VOR has not moved. Hooded eyes lift slowly from the table to the camera over two full seconds. At 0:15 his right hand unweaves from the left and moves to the table — not to the lighter, not to the glass. His fingers settle on the edge of the top black-and-white photograph. He slides it forward across the scarred metal with a dry scratch, an inch, two inches, until it sits alone in the center of the table between him and where JAX stands. Face angled up, half in shadow. His hand returns to his lap.
At 0:18 VOR speaks, mouth barely moving, graveled and slow, quieter than JAX — a man who has never needed to raise his voice: "Your brother was very talkative..." A full second of dead air. The right corner of his mouth pulls up in a cold half-smile that does not reach his eyes. "...before he died." On "died" his head tilts perhaps five degrees. The bodyguard inhales audibly through his nose.
SOUND: Same room tone. Old chair creaks as VOR shifts minutely. Photograph scratching metal — dry, deliberate. Suit fabric whisper. At 0:12 a single low cello long tone begins — one bare note, no melody. On "died" the cello dips a half-step into dissonance. No lighter sound. No flame.

[0:20] HARD CUT TO:

[0:20-0:30] SHOT 3 — CLOSE-UP, eye level, JAX. Based on reference image 1 but framed tighter: brows to chin.
Sound bridge: cello note and room tone continue.
Slow push-in from close-up toward extreme close-up over ten seconds — so slow the viewer barely registers it. JAX has not moved since Shot 1.
Micro-expression sequence — involuntary, anatomically real, no cartoonish reactions:
0:21 — One slow deliberate blink, slower than normal, as if processing. When eyes reopen the gaze is colder, locked on something beyond the lens.
0:22 — The masseter muscle on his right jaw clenches once, a knot rising and falling under stubble. Lips press together for a beat.
0:23 — A single deeper breath through the nose; nostrils flare slightly; the tendon on the right side of his neck stands out for one pulse. He swallows; Adam's apple rises and falls.
0:24 — The left corner of his mouth pulls up very slowly — not a smile, a baring of teeth, asymmetrical, colder than VOR's half-smile. Reaches full expression at 0:25.
0:25 — JAX speaks, lower than before, almost a whisper but each word cuts: "Then he told you..." A pause. Chin lifts a fraction. "...where to find me."
0:27 — On the last word his eyes flicker off-lens for a fraction of a second toward where VOR sits, then snap back to camera — the movement of a man who has just confirmed a trap. The half-smile vanishes. Face goes neutral: not relaxation, the readiness of a man who has done this before.
0:28 — Outside, distant tire screech on concrete. Two heavy van doors slide open. JAX's eyes widen the smallest amount — not fear, anticipation. Behind him in the blurred background the four men shift; one set of footsteps moves.
0:29.5 — The hanging bulb pops with a flash and dies.
CUT TO BLACK.
SOUND: Cello crescendos, joined by a second cello a perfect fifth above. Slow heartbeat enters at 62bpm, distant. On the tire screech the music cuts mid-note. Heartbeat stops. Bulb pop — a tinkle of glass — then VACUUM SILENCE for one beat. Over the black: the dry, unmistakable schnick of a Zippo opening, one flint strike, a breath of flame, then clink shut — somewhere in the dark. Fade to silence.

AUDIO DESIGN: All dialogue close-mic'd with natural concrete reverb. Sub-bass drone under entire piece rising from -30dB to -20dB. Foleys: boot scuffs, old chair creak, photograph on metal, suit fabric rustle, bulb filament hum, distant water drip, cigarette ember crackle, the single Zippo at the very end only. No jump scares. No stingers. No braams. Terror lives in silence and sub-bass. Wide dynamic range; the tire screech at 0:28 is the loudest moment.

During Shot 2, the briefcase nameplate is plain brushed aluminum under amber light, without letters, engraving or logos. No text. No subtitles. No watermark.

NEGATIVE: No electronic devices. No phones. No radios. No timers. No clocks. No digital numbers. No red lights. No blinking LEDs. No wires. No screens. No lighters being played with. No flames except the single Zippo strike in the final black. No one fidgets. No one toys with objects. No grinning. No exaggerated expressions. No glowing eyes. No color-changing irises. No morphing. No deformation. No flickering. No ghosting. No identity drift. No plastic skin. No symmetry. No airbrushed faces.

TECHNICAL: Photorealistic humans. Natural skin texture with pores, subsurface scattering, capillaries, five-o'clock shadow, slight under-eye bags, lip dryness, natural facial oil. Natural blink rate. Eyes are moist but never glow or change color. Micro-expressions subtle and anatomically credible. Realistic physics. 4K cinematic. 24fps. 35mm anamorphic lens characteristics: oval bokeh, horizontal lens flares, edge softness. Same actor faces preserved exactly across all cuts.

SOUND: Cello crescendos, joined by a second cello a perfect fifth above. Slow heartbeat enters at 62bpm, distant. On the tire screech the music cuts mid-note. Heartbeat stops. Bulb pop — a tinkle of glass — then VACUUM SILENCE for one beat. Over the black: the dry, unmistakable schnick of a Zippo opening, one flint strike, a breath of flame, then clink shut — somewhere in the dark. Fade to silence.

AUDIO DESIGN: All dialogue close-mic'd with natural concrete reverb. Sub-bass drone under entire piece rising from -30dB to -20dB. Foleys: boot scuffs, old chair creak, photograph on metal, suit fabric rustle, bulb filament hum, distant water drip, cigarette ember crackle, the single Zippo at the very end only. No jump scares. No stingers. No braams. Terror lives in silence and sub-bass. Wide dynamic range; the tire screech at 0:28 is the loudest moment.
